Confirmed on current tree: postgres's SelectCandidates carries an extra 'AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rimsky_wait_set w WHERE ... drained_at IS NULL)' clause that sqlite's SelectCandidates lacks entirely (sqlite candidate query has no wait-set predicate at all). wait-set dossier states the upstream-dependency predicate 'is fully resolved by the row being in stale at all' and dispatch eligibility is 'checked once at that transition' (pending->stale), not re-checked at dispatch-time SELECT. Since a stale row is guaranteed drained, the postgres clause is redundant when the invariant holds but creates a silent cross-backend behavioral asymmetry if it ever doesn't (Plumbline: one idiom repo-wide). fix-code: delete the postgres clause (or add the same guard plus a conformance test to sqlite) to restore parity.

Confirmed on current tree: both backends still map a unique-violation on the content-hash id to shared.ErrTemplateInUse -> HTTP 409. template dossier's Net position states 'Re-registering the same spec is idempotent' as a persistence-layer property. The register handler's GetByHash pre-check masks this in the common case (200 for an already-registered identical spec), narrowing real-world impact to a concurrent identical-register race -- hence minor, not major. fix-code: switch the insert to ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING / an already-exists no-op signal at the persistence layer so the property holds unconditionally, not just when the handler happens to pre-check.

Verified current design corpus delegation.md:25: 'The delegate target MUST be a sub-graph (with both entry and exit declared) reachable in the template; an unknown or non-sub-graph target is rejected,' stated alongside sibling invariants explicitly scoped to template validation. Confirmed on current tree: validateHolds still only checks `declared[from]` -- membership in the map of every node type declared anywhere in the template -- with no upstream/subscription-reachability check, while emitting the error slug 'holds_from_not_dependency' that claims a dependency check was performed. claim-co-holdership dossier's Net position: '`from:` must reference an upstream dependency, keeping the co-holdership graph acyclic.' Runtime resolution (runner_acquire_holders.go's findInstanceNodeByType) likewise resolves any node of that type with no upstream check. Only test coverage is an undeclared-node-type case ("ghost"), not a downstream/disconnected-node case. fix-code: extend holds_from validation to require an actual upstream-dependency relationship, and correct the error slug to match what's actually checked in the interim if partial.

executor dossier's Intentional absences explicitly list 'retry_after_error as a dispatchable prior disposition' as retired ('Retries are in-place; no new row, nothing writes it'), matching node-run dossier's retirement of the whole prior_dispatch-disposition machinery. No production path writes PRIOR_RETRY_AFTER_ERROR (only an unreachable decode case remains); the enum and its proto comments describe a dispatch that can no longer occur. Per rules.md ('pre-v1, delete dead code rather than carrying it forward'), this is dead surface, not documentation-only drift. fix-code: remove the dead enum value (or mark reserved) and its stale comments from executor.proto, and delete the unreachable decode case in runner_dispatch.go.

Confirmed on current tree: emitKeyRevoked still discards the transaction error via `_ = tables.Transaction(...)` and the two marshal-failure branches still bare-return with no log. event-log dossier's Net position: 'Audit/event writes are durable, synchronous, and never silently dropped' (reinforced by the corrections record: the per-request audit row was made synchronous/durable precisely to close this class of gap, and the control-api twin logs 'audit.insert' at error on failure). fix-code: log at error on every failure branch in auth_sweep's audit-write path, matching audit.go::insertEvent's pattern.

Confirmed: auto_terminal.go still carries @concept: claim-handle, @concept: error-policy, and @concept: signal annotations but never @concept: auto-terminal, despite this file being the primary enforcement site for CheckAndFireResolution and the held-terminal resolution/poison-rule invariants that the auto-terminal dossier and concept doc describe. Confirmed on current tree: acquireFanOutIfDeclared's guard is `rs.ParentNodeRunID != nil`, but child_execution.go's DispatchChildren sets ParentNodeRunID on every child scope it creates -- both fan-out partitions AND sub-graph delegation scopes -- so a fan_out declared on a node running inside a sub-graph is silently skipped. fan-out dossier's actual intended guard is narrower: 'runs acquired in a non-main RunScope never fan out again' is meant to stop fan-out CHILDREN (partition-scope runs) from re-fanning-out, not to blanket-suppress fan-out for every scope with any parent (sub-graph delegation is a distinct, orthogonal mechanism per the delegation dossier -- 'a cloned fan-out node can itself delegate'). fix-code: narrow the guard to key off RunScope kind (fan-out-partition) rather than mere parent presence.

Confirmed on current tree: applyErrorPolicy's give_up branch still unconditionally transitions running/stale -> Failed with the run's own error class and cascades via emitSignalInTxOnce with no held/portfolio check, unlike the success-settle path (runner_terminal.go's held probe + portfolio/poison logic). auto-terminal dossier: 'A held run never receives an error: held is post-executor, idle, waiting for commit/abandon; errors happen while running' and the poison rule requires holders to transition to held->failed only via CheckAndFireResolution's portfolio walk with the deferred cascade filtered to non-members. fix-code: route an errored held-subgraph member's give_up through the same held/portfolio/poison mechanism the success path uses, not a raw unfiltered failed cascade.

Confirmed on current tree: resolveLinkedSubClaimsInTx still reads sibling rows via a plain (non-locking) ListByNodeRun, gates only on row.State != Active, and calls ResolveClaimHandleTerminal (which fires the producer verb before any row-guarded write) with no lock; releaseClaim similarly has no state check. cancel-siblings dossier states the LockForUpdate in the cancel walk 'closes the race against a parallel worker on the same supervisor that may be terminating the sibling natively' -- but the native path it must close against remains unlocked, so a concurrent native Commit and a forced cancel-walk Abandon can both reach the producer for one claim_id under Postgres read-committed. fix-code: take the sibling row lock before the native terminal path fires the producer verb, so the two paths actually serialize as the invariant claims.
